nodes.name: Hydrothermal VO2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: 30 mL of deionized water was added to 0.8 g of ammonium metavanadate (NH4VO3) and 2.484 g of anhydrous oxalic acid (H2C2O4), stirred for 30 min, and then, 0.246 g of methylamine (C6H12N4) was added to the above solution. After that, the solution containing 3 cm × 3 cm CC was transferred to a 50 mL autoclave and reacted at 180°C for 12 h. VO2/CC was obtained after natural cooling, washing, and drying. (Figure S1)

nodes.characterization_summary: Pure Co₃O₄ and V₂O₅ on CC indexed to crystalline phases Co₃O₄ (PDF#43-1003) and V₂O₅ (PDF#41-1426); Co₃O₄-VOₓ shows characteristic peaks at 28.9° and 29.5° corresponding to (002) and (-401) planes of VO₂ (PDF#31-1438).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structure of the prepared catalysts was analyzed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) spectroscopy (Figure 1b). The pure Co₃O₄ and V₂O₅ on CC can be indexed to the crystalline phase of Co₃O₄ (PDF#43-1003) and V₂O₅ (PDF#41-1426), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₃O₄-VOₓ shows two vibration peaks corresponding to VO₂ at 825 and 919 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, in the Raman spectrum of Co₃O₄-VOₓ (Figure 1c), two vibration peaks corresponding to VO₂ also appeared at 825 and 919 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: V₂O₅ exhibits leaf-like structure; Co₃O₄ possesses petal-like nanosheets; Co₃O₄-VOₓ morphologies consistent with VO₂, indicating Co(OH)₂ growing underneath VOₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be found from Figure 1d,e that V₂O₅ exhibits a leaf-like structure, while Co₃O₄ possesses petal-like nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₃O₄-VOₓ shows Co (18.9%), V (24.8%), O (56.3%) confirming Co₃O₄ growing underneath VOₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be seen from the energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) element mapping (Figures 1g and S3) that the signal corresponding to Co (18.9%) is weaker than those of V (24.8%) and O (56.3%).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₃O₄-VOₓ shows electron transfer from Co to V through Co-O-V bonds; after 12h CP test, surface Oᵥ content increased from 18.9% to 22.9%; Co 2p binding energy shift minimal indicating stability; V species undetectable due to VOₓ dissolution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) results demonstrate that electrons are transferred from Co to V through Co-O-V bridging bonds (Figure S10). And the surface content of Oᵥ on Co₃O₄-VOₓ increased from 18.9 to 22.9% after the CP test (Figure 3j).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₃O₄-VOₓ gradually converts to Co(OH)₂ during HER electrolysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With further research, it is found that in the process of electrolysis, Co₃O₄ will be gradually converted to Co(OH)₂, while VOₓ will be dissolved in the electrolyte, and the final product is Co(OH)₂ (Figure 3a).

nodes.characterization_summary: After 40th CV cycle, VOₓ layer on Co₃O₄-VOₓ surface begins to collapse exposing underlying Co₃O₄ with Co(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3b, after the 40th CV scan, the VOₓ layer on the surface begins to collapse, and Co₃O₄ with Co(OH)₂ at the bottom of the VOₓ is gradually exposed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co(OH)₂ nanosheets ~300 nm length, ~4.0 nm thickness after 12h CP test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image shows that the length of the nanosheet is about 300 nm... The Co(OH)₂ nanosheets with a thickness of about 4.0 nm were obtained after conducting the CP test for 12 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co(OH)₂ shows interplanar spacings of 0.238 nm (102), 0.447 nm (002), and 0.282 nm matching Co(OH)₂ PDF#51-1731.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The planes with interplanar spacings of 0.238 and 0.447 nm in high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) correspond to the (102) and (002) planes of Co(OH)₂, respectively.
In addition, the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Figure 3f) further demonstrates that Co(OH)₂ has a polycrystalline structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₃O₄-VOₓ shows Co₃O₄ phonon modes E_g (~528 cm⁻¹), F₂g (~572 cm⁻¹), A₁g (~734 cm⁻¹); at -0.15 V vs RHE peak at 924 cm⁻¹ (symmetric stretching of (V₁₀O₂₈)⁶⁻ or terminal V=O); at -0.22 V vs RHE peak at 820 cm⁻¹ (antisymmetric stretching).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co₃O₄-VOₓ showed three characteristic Raman peaks after immersion in the electrolyte, corresponding to E_g (~528 cm⁻¹), F₂g (~572 cm⁻¹), and A₁g (~734 cm⁻¹) phonon modes of Co₃O₄ spinel oxide.

nodes.characterization_summary: V content stabilizes at ~0.5 mM after 30 min during CP test; 0.56 mM after 12h soaking.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2c, the content of Co remained at a low level, while V increased rapidly during the first 30 min until it stabilized at about 0.5 mM for 120 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₃O₄-VOₓ has charge transfer resistance R_ct = 1.235 Ω (vs Co₃O₄ 17.18 Ω, closest to Pt/C 0.8106 Ω); solution resistance R_s ≈ 3.0 Ω for all catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co₃O₄-VOₓ possesses the smallest charge transfer resistance (R_ct, 1.235Ω) in contrast to CC (223.3Ω), V₂O₅ (175.8Ω), and Co₃O₄ (17.18Ω), which is closer to 20% Pt/C (0.8106).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₃O₄-VOₓ ECSA = 667.5 cm² (~11× Co₃O₄); j_ECSA and exchange current density j₀ = 0.72 mA cm⁻² superior to Co₃O₄ (j₀ = 0.05 mA cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the CV curves at different scan rates (Figure S14), the electrochemical active area (ECSA) of Co₃O₄-VOₓ was calculated to be 667.5 cm² (Table S2), which is about 11 times than that of Co₃O₄.
